sections.h2: Where is the Perry County recorder and how does the office work?
sections.html:
The Perry County Recorder is at 212 S. Main Street in New Lexington, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm, with a phone line at (740) 342-2494. The county auditor works from the same building at the same hours.

The recorder's page describes the office as the keeper of land records: ownership, title transfers and mortgage histories. Staff do not search titles for the public and do not give legal advice, but the records are open, and you can sit down and look through them yourself.

The office takes cash and checks only. It does not take credit cards, so plan the payment before you send a document in.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Perry County?
sections.html:
The recorder's own answer is $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each page after that. A $20.00 charge is added for a document that does not follow the layout rules, and a $4.00 marginal reference fee is added for documents that need a reference to an earlier record.

Recording charges quoted on the Perry County Recorder page
ItemCharge
First two pages$34.00
Each page after the second$8.00
Non-compliant layout (3 inch top margin on page one, 1 inch on sides and bottom)$20.00 added
Document needing a reference$4.00 added
Payment methodsCash or check

Ohio's recording statute, Revised Code 317.32, also lets a county charge a preservation surcharge of up to $5. Ask the recorder whether it applies to your document, because the Perry page does not list one.

sections.h2: What does the Perry County auditor collect when a house sells?
sections.html:
The auditor transfers the property on the tax list before the recorder records the deed. The grantee or the grantee's representative submits a statement of value, and the seller pays the conveyance fee.

Under section 319.54(G)(3), the state fee is one dollar, or ten cents for each one hundred dollars or fraction of one hundred dollars of value, whichever is greater. Counties may also levy a real property transfer tax under section 322.02 of up to thirty cents per hundred dollars, so the total at your closing depends on what Perry County has adopted.

The Perry County Auditor's website has a Conveyance Fee Calculator that includes the parcel transfer fee. Enter the parcel count and the sale price and read the result off the county's own tool. The auditor's Forms page also carries the state conveyance forms.

sections.h2: How do you search Perry County land records?
sections.html:
The recorder offers an online index called Adaptable Visual Access. It gives the volume and page number for each document type, but the page says the actual documents and images are not online. To get a copy, call or email the office for payment options and fees.

Two services are free to owners. The office signs up property owners for a fraud alert from its software company, which notifies a subscriber within 24 business hours of any document recorded against the name. The recorder cannot stop a document that meets the filing rules, so the alert is a warning rather than a block.

Veterans can bring an original or certified DD214 and a photo ID to record it, and the office also issues veteran ID cards.

sections.h2: Which documents does the Perry County recorder file besides deeds?
sections.html:
Section 317.08 sends a long list of instruments into the official records. For a house seller, the ones that matter most are these:

  • Mortgages, with their amendments and extensions.
  • Land contracts that run longer than a year, and leases or memoranda of lease.
  • Powers of attorney, which an agent may use to sign for a seller.
  • Mechanic's liens, federal tax liens and other recorded liens.
  • Options to purchase, which are only recorded when they state a specific day and year of expiration.

The recorder files documents in the order they are presented. A transfer on death designation affidavit is recorded the same way as a deed, at the deed fee, and it must be on record before the owner dies to be effective.

sections.h2: What should a Perry County seller fix before the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Most recording problems come from small mistakes in the paperwork. Check these items before you sign:

  • The deed is signed and acknowledged before an officer named in section 5301.01, such as a notary public.
  • The deed carries the grantee's address and a reference to the last recorded instrument, which section 319.20 requires.
  • The page margins match the layout rules, so the $20.00 charge does not apply.
  • You know the mortgage payoff. After payoff, the lender sends a release to be recorded, and the recorder says it can give you a copy.
  • You have a way to pay in cash or by check, since there is no card option.

If a spouse has died and you need to remove the name from a deed, the recorder only records documents and cannot prepare them, so an attorney has to draft the paperwork.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Perry County housing?
sections.html:
Perry County had 35,918 residents in July 2025, up 1.4% from the April 2020 estimates base, spread over about 408 square miles of land. The Census Bureau lists 15,173 housing units and 13,452 households.

  • Owner-occupied rate: 76.4%.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $191,100.
  • Median gross rent: $777 a month.
  • Mean travel time to work: 33.2 minutes.
  • Building permits in 2025: 39.
  • Persons in poverty: 13.7%.

The 33.2 minute commute is the longest of the three counties in this Census comparison. Wikipedia places the county in the Columbus metropolitan area.

sections.h2: How is property valued in Perry County?
sections.html:
The auditor says Ohio requires a countywide reappraisal every six years and a state-issued percentage update in the third year between reappraisals. The office lists about 31,000 parcels for 2024. Property classes are residential, agricultural, commercial and industrial.

The auditor's site also announced that House Bill 479 provides a fixed-amount, one-time property tax reduction for current recipients of the Standard and Enhanced Homestead Exemptions, applying to tax year 2026 or, for manufactured and mobile homes, tax year 2027. Ask the auditor how that credit is applied if you sell during the year.

If storm or flood damage changes what a house is worth, call the auditor at (740) 342-2074 and ask how a damaged-property adjustment works.

sections.h2: Which communities and landmarks shape Perry County sales?
sections.html:
Perry County was established on March 1, 1818 from parts of Fairfield, Washington and Muskingum counties. New Lexington is the county seat and the largest city. The villages are Corning, Crooksville, Glenford, Hemlock, Junction City, New Straitsville, Rendville, Roseville (partly in the county), Shawnee, Somerset and Thornville.

Part of Wayne National Forest lies inside the county, and neighbors include Licking, Muskingum, Morgan, Athens, Hocking and Fairfield counties.

faqs.q: Does the Perry County Recorder accept credit cards?
faqs.a: No. The recorder's page says the office accepts only cash and checks.

faqs.q: Can I view recorded deeds online in Perry County?
faqs.a: You can see an index online, with volume and page numbers, but not the document images. Call or email the recorder to get a copy and ask about payment and fees.

faqs.q: What is the Perry County recording fee for a deed?
faqs.a: The recorder quotes $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each additional page. A $20.00 charge is added for a document with non-compliant margins, and $4.00 is added when a document needs a reference.

faqs.q: Where do I find the conveyance fee in Perry County?
faqs.a: Use the Conveyance Fee Calculator on the Perry County Auditor's website, which includes the parcel transfer fee. The auditor's office at 212 S. Main Street can confirm the amount.

faqs.q: Can the recorder tell me whether my title is clear?
faqs.a: No. The office cannot search titles or give legal advice. You can search the public records in person, or hire an attorney or a title company.
